stem: A grower uses a fixed amber-trichome percentage as a universal harvest rule for every cultivar. What is the strongest scientific concern?
choices: Trichome maturation can vary with genotype, plant age, and sampling position, so one fixed percentage may not generalize across crops
A fixed amber percentage can standardize records across cultivars, making differences in developmental context less important for harvest comparison
Trichome color provides a direct maturity measurement, so representative sampling adds little once a numerical threshold has been established
Cultivar-specific flowering duration can be combined with one amber threshold to remove most uncertainty caused by canopy-position differences
rationale: Research shows genotype and plant age influence glandular-trichome development and maturation. A single universal color threshold can oversimplify those differences.
